answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires agents to cross a steep fee ridge by staking tokens to participate. If any identity misbehaves, verifiable proofs let validators burn cryptographic stake directly. Generating new identities scales with superlinear cost O(n^1.5), preventing adversaries who attempt to forge synthetic consensus. Each agent records operations with a deterministic cryptographic quill, making massive cloned identities mathematically unaffordable.
